title: Far away, yet the closest match?
hook: One arrow is far off, one is right next door. Which is more alike by cosine?

knows: that an embedding places an item as a point or arrow in space
doesNotKnow: that cosine similarity compares only the direction of two arrows
that a far-away arrow can be a perfect cosine match

misconception: Similar means close together in a straight line.
objective: The learner can say that cosine similarity ignores length, so an arrow far away in the same direction scores 1.00 while a nearby arrow at an angle scores lower.

claims.text: The vectors Q = (1, 1), B = (k, k) and C = (1, 0.2) are a toy, labelled 'Toy 2-D vectors' on the stage.
claims.source: Brief 42 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; Q, C, bAt in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: B = (k, k) has cosine 1.00 with Q for every length k from 1 to 10; its straight-line distance from Q is 1.4 × (k − 1): 12.7 at (10, 10), 9.9 at (8, 8).
claims.source: cos(Q, kQ) = k|Q|² / (|Q| · k|Q|) = 1. node: cosine 1.00 and dist sqrt(2)(k−1) for k = 1..10 (12.73 at 10, 9.90 at 8).

claims.text: C = (1, 0.2) is 0.8 from Q but has cosine 0.83 with it, so by distance C is closer and by cosine B is more similar.
claims.source: cos = (1·1 + 1·0.2) / (sqrt 2 · sqrt 1.04) = 1.2 / 1.442 = 0.832; |Q − C| = 0.8. node re-run in the build session.

claims.text: Cosine similarity is the dot product divided by the two lengths, so it measures the angle between arrows and ignores their length (1 = same direction).
claims.source: Manning, Raghavan & Schütze 2008, Introduction to Information Retrieval, §6.3 (cosine similarity, length normalisation).

claims.text: Some real systems compare text embeddings by cosine similarity, so a longer document about the same topic can still match.
claims.source: About real systems: Mikolov et al. 2013, 'Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases' (NeurIPS) compare word vectors by cosine; Manning et al. 2008 §6.3 motivates length normalisation with a document and its doubled copy. 'Some', not all.

recall.question: Two documents' embedding arrows point in exactly the same direction, but one arrow is three times longer. Their cosine similarity is:
options: 1/3, because one is three times longer
recall.why: Cosine depends only on the angle between the arrows. Stretching an arrow does not change its direction, so the score stays at 1.
